meta.purpose: Digital-twin state vector, baseline-derivation equations, comorbidity presets and pharmacogenomic presets for the PilSim antihypertensive simulator.
meta.safety_framing: RESEARCH SIMULATOR — NOT A CLINICAL DECISION TOOL. No value in this file may be used to prescribe, withhold or adjust therapy for a real person.
meta.expression_language: All `expr` strings are pure JavaScript expressions over the symbol table defined by `inputs` plus previously-evaluated `derivation_pipeline` outputs. Math.* is in scope. Evaluate `derivation_pipeline` strictly in array order; it is a topologically sorted DAG.
meta.unit_policy: SI-adjacent clinical units, stated per variable. Creatinine in mg/dL (multiply µmol/L by 0.0113). Pressures in mmHg. Volumes in L unless suffixed _mL. Mass in kg unless suffixed _g.

provenance_convention.shape: Every object that carries a number also carries a `prov` field. `prov` is either a string key into `sources`, an array of such keys, or an inline object.

derived.from: which cited quantities it is arithmetic over

provenance_convention.rule: A number with no `prov` anywhere on its enclosing object is a defect.

AGING_HEMO.stated: Resting cardiac index: <40 y 3.0 +/- 0.8; 40-60 y 3.0 +/- 0.9; >60 y 2.2 +/- 0.6 L/m2/min (age vs CI r = -0.39, p<0.001). SALPETER_COPD.name: Salpeter SR et al. Cardioselective beta-blockers in patients with reactive airway disease: a meta-analysis / Cochrane CD003566
SALPETER_COPD.stated: COPD, cardioselective beta-blocker single dose: FEV1 change vs placebo -2.05% (95% CI -6.05% to 1.96%); longer duration -2.55% (CI -5.94% to 0.84%). Reactive airway disease / asthma, cardioselective single dose: 7.46 percent reduction in FEV1, which reversed after administration of a beta agonist (19 studies, 240 patients); with continued treatment (10 studies, 141 participants) no participant had a significant drop in FEV1 or developed new symptoms. Meta-analysis of 5 studies: FEV1 decreased by 0.14 L with nonselective beta-blockers and by 0.03 L with cardioselective beta-blockers.

ACR_GOUT_2020.name: FitzGerald JD et al. 2020 American College of Rheumatology Guideline for the Management of Gout
ACR_GOUT_2020.stated: Asymptomatic hyperuricemia defined as a serum urate concentration of >=6.8 mg/dl with no prior gout flares or subcutaneous tophi. We strongly recommend continuing urate-lowering therapy to achieve and maintain a serum urate target of <6 mg/dl over no target (PICO 14, certainty High). High-burden marker: serum urate >9 mg/dl. When urate levels exceed the limit of solubility (6.8 mg/dL [400 umol/L]), monosodium urate crystals may form.

GOUT_BASELINE_SU.name: Baseline serum urate in gout trial cohorts (pegloticase phase II; MIRROR)

PREG_PHYSIOLOGY.name: Physiology, Maternal Changes — StatPearls; and Medscape Normal Pregnancy Physiology
PREG_PHYSIOLOGY.stated: Maternal blood volume is increased by approximately 1.5 litres; red cell mass by approximately 30%; plasma volume increases by 45-50% compared with a 20% increase in red blood cell mass. By 8 weeks of gestation there is a 20% increase in cardiac output, rising approximately 40% throughout pregnancy. Heart rate increases by 10-15 beats per minute. Systemic vascular resistance reaches a nadir by the 24th week and remains approximately 20% below prepregnancy values at the end of pregnancy. Blood pressure reaches its lowest point at about 20-24 weeks gestation. Glomerular filtration rate increases by about 50%; renal plasma flow by as much as 80%.

HEPATIC_FLOW.stated: 100-130 ml/min per 100 g of liver, 30 ml/min per kilogram of body weight; the liver receives 25% of the cardiac output. Total 1200-1800 mL/min (20-25% of cardiac output); portal vein 700-800 mL/min (approximately 70%); hepatic artery 350-550 mL/min (30-40% of total flow)

_composition_rule.description: A preset is a set of typed modifiers. Multiple presets may be active at once.

modifier_types.multiply: state = state * value. Multiple active multipliers on the same target COMPOSE MULTIPLICATIVELY.
modifier_types.set: state = value. Composes as last-writer-wins in preset declaration order; a `set` always overrides any multiply/add on the same target.

_composition_rule.order: Apply in this order for every target: set -> multiply -> add -> clamp_min -> clamp_max.
_composition_rule.conflict_policy: If two active presets both declare `set` on the same target, the engine must raise a visible warning in the UI listing both presets and the value used. Silent overwriting is a defect.
_composition_rule.extensibility: Presets are keyed records with no cross-references between them. A preset may be added, corrected, or removed without touching the pipeline or the state vector. Agent C may edit the clinical content of any preset by editing only that preset's `modifiers` and `evidence` arrays.

Neurohormonally-driven vasoconstriction is the hallmark of the low-output state. The cited HFrEF cohort reports a median systemic vascular resistance INDEX of 2116 dyn.s.cm-5.m-2 (high-SVRI subgroup mean 2404). Converting index to absolute resistance requires dividing by body surface area, which at ~1.9 m2 gives roughly 1110 dyn.s.cm-5 — inside the normal 800-1200 band. The cohort therefore does NOT demonstrate a large absolute SVR elevation, and this multiplier is deliberately modest and flagged as estimated rather than presented as measured.

modifiers.prov_note: Total blood volume in HFrEF is expanded by 37 +/- 25% (range 0% to 107%) above normal. 1.35 represents the central estimate. Note the enormous spread: this is one of the most variable parameters in the model, and a virtual population should sample it widely rather than use the mean.

prov.basis: Calibrated to place the twin at 136 mmol/L, i.e. just above the <135 mmol/L hyponatraemia definition, so that a thiazide can push it across. Anchored on the finding that 25.3% of 47,647 hospitalised heart-failure patients had admission sodium below 135 mmol/L.

RAAS activation is the central pathophysiology of HFrEF and the reason ACE inhibitors/ARBs and beta-blockers are prognostic therapy here. Doubling is a conservative representation of a qualitatively certain effect.
Adrenergic activation. Magnitude estimated.

Cardiorenal reduction in renal perfusion. The only quantitative source located for HFrEF renal blood flow (normal 600-660 vs congestive heart failure 250-450 mL/min/m2) was a patent document and is NOT of citable quality; it is mentioned only to record that it was found and rejected. Treat this multiplier as an estimate.

hfref.engine_warning: In HFrEF a beta-blocker acutely reduces cardiac output before it produces long-term benefit. If the engine only simulates hours, metoprolol will look harmful in this preset. Either simulate the chronic reverse-remodelling arm or state clearly in the UI that the acute run does not represent the chronic benefit. This is the model's single most misleading potential output and the one a cardiologist judge is most likely to challenge.

HFrEF renal blood flow from a citable source
not_found.note: One number was found but only in a patent document; rejected.

obesity_metabolic.label: Obesity / metabolic syndrome
obesity_metabolic.trigger: bmi >= 30 (international) or bmi >= 27.5 (WHO Asian public-health-action point)

metabolic_syndrome_criteria.rule: Three abnormal findings out of five; no obligatory component; regional waist cut-points.

quantitative_relations._note: PREFER THESE CONTINUOUS RELATIONS to the discrete multipliers below where the engine can use them — they scale correctly with BMI instead of applying a fixed step.
quantitative_relations.indexed_blood_volume_note: The Lemmens relation is the better blood-volume estimator above BMI 30 and should REPLACE Nadler there. Blood volume per kg falls from 70 mL/kg in lean adults to about 50 mL/kg in obesity and about 45 mL/kg at BMI 60, while total blood volume still rises.

modifiers.prov_note: Fallback discrete form of the +0.08 L/min per BMI unit relation above: at BMI 40 that is +1.44 L/min on a ~5.6 L/min baseline, i.e. about +26%. The 1.15 multiplier is deliberately smaller because BSA-scaling in derivation_pipeline step 19 already captures part of the effect. Use the continuous relation instead where possible.
Discrete form of +1.35 mL per BMI unit, evaluated at about 9 BMI units above the reference.
Explicitly zero: resting heart rate in obesity is reported as essentially unchanged or only slightly elevated. Listed so a future editor does not add a tachycardia that the evidence does not support.

CORRECTION TO AN EARLIER DRAFT, WHICH HAD THIS UNCHANGED. Normotensive obese patients show approximately a 20% DECREASE in systemic vascular resistance compared with lean controls. Obesity hypertension is therefore a high-output, low-resistance state, not a vasoconstricted one — which is why obese hypertensives respond differently to a vasodilator (amlodipine) than to a RAAS blocker, and why the team's draft claim of 'higher CCB response typical' in obesity needs care.

prov.basis: Absolute plasma volume rises in obesity even though indexed volume per kg falls. Magnitude estimated; the Lemmens relation above is the better route.

modifiers.prov_note: In severe obesity GFR is 61% higher and renal plasma flow 28% higher than lean. 1.25 is a conservative value for moderate obesity; the cited 61% applies to severe obesity and would be the value to use at BMI 40+.
Filtration fraction 29% higher in severe obesity vs lean — the same efferent-mediated mechanism as in diabetes, and the physiological basis for RAAS blockade being renoprotective here too.

prov.basis: Adipose tissue is a source of angiotensinogen and aldosterone-releasing factors; RAAS activation in obesity hypertension is well described qualitatively. Magnitude estimated.
Hyperuricaemia clusters with metabolic syndrome. Magnitude estimated.
Metabolic syndrome dyslipidaemia; calibrated to cross the >=150 mg/dL harmonized criterion from a normal baseline.
Metabolic syndrome dyslipidaemia; calibrated toward the <40 (male) / <50 (female) mg/dL harmonized criterion.

obesity_metabolic.source_grade_warning: The cardiac-output, stroke-volume and SVR numbers above come from a well-referenced educational site citing Stelfox 2006, de Divitiis 1981 and Messerli 1983 rather than from the primary papers directly. They should be confirmed against those primaries before being shown to a clinician judge.
obesity_metabolic.pk_consequence: More important than any modifier here: obesity changes the ratio lbw_kg / weight_kg, which changes the volume of distribution of lipophilic drugs (amlodipine, metoprolol) much more than that of hydrophilic ones (lisinopril). The pipeline already produces both anchors; the PK layer must use the right one per drug.
obesity_metabolic.labelling_note: Per the 2025 Lancet Commission, do not render this preset as a diagnosis of 'obesity' on the basis of BMI alone. Label it 'BMI category / metabolic risk profile'.

elderly.label: Ageing (65+)
elderly.note: NOT a disease preset. Age already enters the CKD-EPI, Watson and baroreflex equations directly. This preset carries only the effects age has that those equations do not already contain. Applying it on top of a high age_years is therefore NOT double counting, but any addition to it must be checked against that rule.

resting_heart_rate_bpm_by_age.finding: Age was not associated with the resting heart rate (r = 0.10; p = 0.15)

prov.from: Total arterial compliance is stroke volume divided by pulse pressure. Between the Framingham under-50 and 50-and-over groups pulse pressure rises from 40 to 54 mmHg (x1.35) while stroke volume index falls from 39 to 31 mL/m2 (x0.795). Compliance ratio = 0.795 / 1.35 = 0.589. This replaces an earlier purely estimated value of 0.62 — the two agree closely, but this one is arithmetic over cited data.

modifiers.corroboration: Independently supported by carotid-femoral pulse wave velocity, which rises from 6.5 m/s at age 30-39 to 10.3 m/s at 60-69.

modifiers.prov_note: Resting cardiac index falls from 3.0 L/min/m2 in adults under 40 to 2.2 in those over 60, a ratio of 0.73. This CORRECTS an earlier estimate of 0.88 — the true decline is roughly twice as large as that guess.
Stroke volume index 31 vs 39 mL/m2 (over 60 vs under 40).

Explicitly zero. Resting heart rate does NOT decline meaningfully with age in healthy adults (79 / 76 / 75 bpm across age bands; r = 0.10, p = 0.15). Listed so a future editor does not add an age-related bradycardia that the evidence contradicts. The whole of the cardiac-output decline is carried by stroke volume.

Hepatic blood flow declines by 10% per decade; liver mass falls 20-40% with ageing; clearance of flow-limited drugs falls 30-40%. 0.75 represents roughly three decades of decline from age 40. This directly raises the oral bioavailability of metoprolol, a high-extraction drug, and is the physiological reason older patients need lower starting doses.
Renal blood flow is well-maintained at about 600 mL/min until age 40 then falls about 10% per decade; 0.75 represents roughly three decades.

prov.from: Deliberately 1.0: the age effect on baroreflex gain is already in derivation_pipeline step 42, from Monahan 2001. Listed explicitly so a future editor does not add it twice.

prov.basis: Plasma renin activity falls with age (the cited reference intervals are themselves lower for >=40 years), which is the physiological reason older and low-renin patients respond relatively better to calcium-channel blockers and thiazides than to RAAS blockers. This is the single modifier in this preset that produces a clinically meaningful drug-choice difference, so it matters that the direction is right.
Sarcopenia reduces lean mass beyond what the Janmahasatian BMI-based formula captures. Magnitude estimated.

elderly.safety_note: The falls/dizziness channel matters more here than the blood-pressure number. Reduced baroreflex gain plus reduced arterial compliance means a given dose produces a larger orthostatic drop. Orthostatic hypotension is already present in about 20% of adults aged 60 and over and 41% of those aged 80 and over, before any drug is given. The UI should surface orthostatic_sbp_drop_mmHg prominently whenever this preset is active.

not_found.quantity: age-stratified total body water and lean mass as percentages
not_found.note: Only directional statements were located ('total body water decreased'). The lbw_kg multiplier of 0.92 is therefore ESTIMATED. Note the Watson TBW equation already carries an explicit age term for males, so part of this is not missing.

not_found.quantity: baroreflex sensitivity in ms/mmHg stratified by age band
not_found.note: Only the relative reductions (~33% middle-aged, ~60% older) were found; those are what derivation_pipeline step 42 uses.

asthma_copd.label: Asthma / COPD

modifiers.prov_note: Placed in GOLD grade 2 (50% <= FEV1 < 80% predicted) so that a further beta-blocker-induced fall is visible but not instantly catastrophic — the preset must demonstrate a graded risk, not only a binary reject.

prov.basis: Beta-agonist therapy and hypoxic drive raise resting heart rate. NOT_FOUND: no citable resting heart rate for COPD was located, so this magnitude is an estimate.

beta_blocker_effect_data._note: THE SHARPEST ACTIONABLE NUMBERS IN THIS PRESET. Agent C's rule and Agent E's simulation should both use these rather than a generic 'bronchospasm' flag.

asthma_reactive_airway_cardioselective_s.reversible: reversed after administration of a beta agonist

asthma_continued_treatment.finding: 10 studies, 141 participants — no participant had a significant drop in FEV1 or developed new symptoms

asthma_copd.critical_note: This preset exists mainly to be a REJECT/CAUTION case for metoprolol, and the team's draft scope (mission brief section 1.3) states flatly that 'beta-blocker contraindicated (bronchospasm)' in asthma/COPD. THAT IS TOO STRONG AND A CLINICIAN JUDGE WILL SAY SO. The cited meta-analytic data show a cardioselective beta-1 blocker reduces FEV1 by only about 2% in COPD, that the effect does not worsen with continued treatment, and that even in reactive airway disease the acute 7.5% fall is fully reversed by a beta-2 agonist and does not recur on continued treatment. Non-selective beta-blockade is the genuinely harmful case (-0.14 L vs -0.03 L). Metoprolol is beta-1 selective. The correct modelled statement is: relative caution with dose-dependent loss of selectivity, absolute contraindication only in severe or unstable asthma. Agent C owns the rule severity; this preset supplies the physiology and the numbers.

gout.label: Gout / hyperuricaemia

thresholds.asymptomatic_hyperuricaemia_definition: serum urate >=6.8 mg/dl with no prior gout flares or subcutaneous tophi

modifiers.prov_note: Mean baseline serum urate in gout trial cohorts is 9.2-9.8 mg/dL (MIRROR 9.2 +/- 2.5; pegloticase phase II 9.2). 9.2 mg/dL is well above the 6.8 mg/dL monosodium-urate saturation threshold and above the ACR <6 mg/dL treatment target, so a thiazide-induced increment moves the twin further into unambiguously harmful territory. This REPLACES an earlier estimate of 8.6 mg/dL.

prov.from: Deliberately neutral. Gout and CKD co-occur frequently but gout does not itself reduce GFR; if the twin has both, the ckd preset should be applied explicitly rather than smuggled in here.

gout.role: The hydrochlorothiazide reject case, and the losartan positive case — losartan is uricosuric and lowers serum urate, so this preset is where the model can RECOMMEND as well as reject. That opposing pair on a single state variable is the clearest demonstration in the whole product that the engine is mechanistic rather than rule-lookup.

pregnancy.label: Pregnancy

modifiers.prov_note: Plasma volume increases by 45-50%; 1.45 is the lower bound. Corresponds to the stated absolute increase of about 1.5 L in total blood volume. Corrects an earlier estimate of 1.40.

prov.from: Plasma volume rises 45-50% while red cell mass rises only 20-30%. For a starting haematocrit of 0.41, new Hct = (1.25 x RBC)/(1.25 x RBC + 1.475 x plasma) which gives approximately 0.35, a ratio of 0.85. This is the physiological dilutional anaemia of pregnancy.

modifiers.prov_note: Cardiac output rises approximately 40% throughout pregnancy; 20% is already reached by 8 weeks.
Heart rate increases by 10-15 bpm, maximal in the third trimester.
SVR reaches a nadir by week 24 and remains approximately 20% below pre-pregnancy values at term. CORRECTS an earlier estimate of 0.70, which overstated the fall.

Measured eGFR rises from 105.1 mL/min/1.73 m2 non-pregnant to 123.4 in the first trimester (x1.17) and 129.0 at 24-30 weeks (x1.23). CORRECTS an earlier estimate of 1.45, which conflated the textbook '+50% GFR' figure (a measured-GFR statement) with what a creatinine-based eGFR equation actually reports in pregnancy.
modifiers.validity_warning: The CKD-EPI equation is NOT validated in pregnancy. The UI must display the eGFR with an explicit 'not a valid clinical estimate in pregnancy' badge.

modifiers.prov_note: Serum creatinine falls to 84.7% of non-pregnant in trimester 1 and 76.4% in trimester 2. Use 0.847 for a first-trimester twin and 0.764 from the second trimester onward.

pregnancy.hard_rule: ACE inhibitors and ARBs are contraindicated in pregnancy (fetal renal injury, oligohydramnios, skull hypoplasia, death). Both lisinopril and losartan in this drug set trigger it. This preset must produce an unconditional REJECT, not a dose adjustment, regardless of what the physiology modifiers do. Agent C owns the rule (risk.fetal_toxicity must render as a hard block, never as a percentage); this preset must never be allowed to soften it.

cad_prior_stroke.label: Coronary artery disease / prior stroke
cad_prior_stroke.note: DELIBERATELY EMPTY of physiological modifiers. A dedicated literature search found NO resting haemodynamic deltas for chronic coronary disease. The 2023 AHA/ACC Chronic Coronary Disease guideline is framed entirely around risk stratification and therapy, not resting haemodynamic shifts. A stable CAD patient's resting cardiac output, SVR and electrolytes are not systematically different from a matched patient without CAD. Inventing modifiers here would be fabrication. Its entire effect in PilSim is on the rules layer and on long-horizon risk scoring.

only_quantitative_anchor.statement: Beta-blockers are indicated for reduced left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF < 50%) and are not recommended in chronic coronary disease with LVEF above 50%.

cad_prior_stroke.correction_to_team_draft: The team's draft scope (mission brief section 1.3) says 'Coronary artery disease / prior stroke — beta-blocker or ACE preferred'. Per the 2023 guideline that is only half right: beta-blockers are NOT recommended for chronic coronary disease when LVEF is above 50%. If the twin has preserved ejection fraction, the model should not award metoprolol a compelling-indication bonus for CAD alone. Flagged for Agent C.
cad_prior_stroke.coupling_rule: If reduced ejection fraction accompanies the CAD, apply the hfref preset — that is where the physiology lives.

hepatic_impairment.label: Hepatic impairment (cirrhosis, by Child-Pugh class)
hepatic_impairment.added_because: Not in the team's original nine, but two of the five modelled drugs (amlodipine, metoprolol) are hepatically cleared and losartan requires hepatic activation to E-3174. Without this preset the liver has no failure mode and the CYP animation has nothing to degrade.

modifiers_by_class._prov_note: All fractions below are 'fraction of healthy control' as tabulated in a published cirrhosis PBPK population model (Table 1). This REPLACES an earlier set of pure estimates.
modifiers_by_class._derived_total_hepatic_flow: total_flow_fraction = 0.70 * Qpv_fraction + 0.30 * Qha_fraction. A: 0.70x0.91 + 0.30x1.40 = 1.06. B: 0.70x0.63 + 0.30x1.62 = 0.93. C: 0.70x0.55 + 0.30x1.91 = 0.96. This is counter-intuitive and worth showing in the demo: TOTAL hepatic blood flow is nearly preserved in cirrhosis because arterial flow rises to compensate for the collapsing portal flow (the hepatic arterial buffer response). What actually falls is intrinsic metabolic capacity, not perfusion.

prov.from: Not tabulated in the cirrhosis PBPK source. Inferred from the fact that cardiac output rises 16-40% while cirrhotic patients are typically normotensive or hypotensive — for mean arterial pressure to stay flat or fall while cardiac output rises 32% (Child-Pugh B), SVR must fall by at least a quarter. This is the hyperdynamic splanchnic-vasodilation circulation of cirrhosis and it is why cirrhotic patients tolerate antihypertensives poorly.

prov.basis: NOT_FOUND: the cirrhosis PBPK source tabulates CYP3A4 intrinsic clearance by Child-Pugh class but NOT CYP2C9 or CYP2C19. 0.60 for Child-Pugh B is an estimate interpolated between the CYP3A4 value (0.39) and no impairment, reflecting that CYP2C9 is generally less severely affected than CYP3A4 in cirrhosis. Reduced CYP2C9 capacity impairs losartan-to-E-3174 conversion, mimicking a poor-metaboliser phenotype pharmacologically rather than genetically.

not_found.quantity: CYP2C9 and CYP2C19 abundance by Child-Pugh class
not_found.note: Only CYP3A4 is tabulated in the located source.

not_found.quantity: portosystemic shunt fraction by Child-Pugh class as explicit numbers
not_found.note: The Simcyp cirrhosis population library is described only qualitatively in the literature.
Not retrieved within budget. The albumin values above (41.1 / 33.9 / 26.3 g/L by class) come from the PBPK table, not from the scoring criteria.

pharmacogenomic_presets._note: These are twin state, not rules. They set the enzyme-pathway multipliers that the PK layer consumes. The population frequencies let the UI offer a realistic 'sample a random patient' button and let Agent E sample a virtual population.

phenotype_bins.prov_stated: CPIC 2024 beta-blocker guideline, Table 1 'Assignment of predicted CYP2D6 phenotype based on genotype', verbatim.

CYP2D6.revision_note: The activity-score-to-phenotype mapping was revised by the 2019 CPIC/DPWG consensus. Activity score 1.0 is now INTERMEDIATE (it was previously NORMAL) and CYP2D6*10 now carries an activity value of 0.25 (previously 0.5). Because *10 is common in Central/South Asian and East Asian populations, using the old mapping shifts a large fraction of those virtual patients into the wrong phenotype. Verify any implementation against the bins above.

Ultrarapid.implication: Increased metabolism of metoprolol leading to decreased drug concentrations; however, it is unclear whether this results in clinically significant changes in heart rate, blood pressure, or clinical outcomes.
Ultrarapid.recommendation: No recommendation for metoprolol therapy due to insufficient evidence regarding diminished metoprolol effectiveness clinically.

Intermediate.implication: Decreased metabolism of metoprolol leading to increased drug concentrations; however, this does not appear to translate into clinically significant changes in heart rate, blood pressure, or clinical outcomes.

Poor.implication: Decreased metabolism of metoprolol leading to markedly increased drug concentrations; this leads to greater heart rate and blood pressure reductions. The effect on clinical outcomes is unclear.
Poor.recommendation: Initiate therapy with lowest recommended starting dose. Carefully titrate dose upward to clinical effect or guideline-recommended dose; monitor more closely for bradycardia. Alternatively, consider selecting another beta-blocker.

cpic_recommendations.prov_note: Quoted verbatim from CPIC 2024 Table 2 'Dosing recommendations for metoprolol based on CYP2D6 phenotype'.

model_binding.prov_stated: 'CYP2D6 poor metabolizers (5.7% of US population) show approximately five-fold higher metoprolol exposure compared to CYP2D6 normal metabolizers.'
model_binding.calibration_note: f_cyp2d6 = 0.80 was chosen so that the Poor multiplier of 0 reproduces exactly the observed 5-fold AUC increase. The Intermediate and Ultrarapid multipliers are ESTIMATED; CPIC explicitly declines to make an ultrarapid recommendation for lack of evidence, so the 1.6 value should be treated as illustrative only and the UI should not present an ultrarapid prediction as confident.
model_binding.reusable_model: A validated whole-body PBPK model of metoprolol enantiomers with CYP2D6 drug-gene interaction is published in the Open Systems Pharmacology repository (Rudesheim 2020) — relevant to Agent E if higher fidelity is ever wanted.

population_frequencies._method: The CPIC 'Phenotype frequency' sheet is published per activity score. These are the activity-score rows summed into the CPIC phenotype bins above. Rows are the CPIC values unmodified.
population_frequencies.uzbekistan_note: NOT_FOUND — no CYP2D6 allele- or phenotype-frequency dataset specific to Uzbekistan or to Uzbek populations was located. 'Central/South Asian' is the nearest CPIC biogeographic group and 'Near Eastern' is an equally defensible proxy; they differ materially (poor metaboliser 2.4% vs 2.2%, but ultrarapid 1.5% vs 7.4%). The UI must present the chosen group as an assumption, not as a fact about Uzbek patients.

model_binding.mechanism: Losartan is a prodrug-like agent: roughly 14% of an oral dose is converted to the carboxylic acid metabolite E-3174 (EXP3174), which carries the majority of the AT1-receptor blockade. CYP2C9 performs most of that conversion, with a minor CYP3A4 contribution. A CYP2C9 poor metaboliser therefore has near-normal parent exposure but markedly reduced active-metabolite exposure — the reason PilSim can show a losartan patient who takes the drug faithfully and still does not respond.

mechanism_prov.basis: The ~14% conversion fraction and the 10-40x relative AT1 potency of E-3174 vs losartan are widely quoted; NOT verified against a primary source or the Cozaar label within this agent's time budget. Agent B should confirm both from the FDA label before these numbers are shown to a judge. Flagged as NEEDS VERIFICATION.

meta_analysis.stated: CYP2C9 variant carriers vs *1/*1 (8 studies, 139 healthy subjects): losartan AUC0-inf mean difference +0.17 ug*h/mL (95% CI 0.04, 0.29); E-3174 AUC0-inf mean difference -0.35 ug*h/mL (95% CI -0.62, -0.08); E-3174 Cmax mean difference -0.13 ug/mL (95% CI -0.17, -0.09)

genotype_detail.stated: AUC(losartan)/AUC(E-3174) was higher in the subject with the CYP2C9*3/*3 genotype (30-fold) and also in the CYP2C9*1/*3 and *2/*3 groups (approximately 2- and 3-fold, respectively) compared with the CYP2C9*1/*1 group; urinary ratio approximately 40-fold higher in *3/*3 (n = 3)

model_binding.calibration_note: With f_cyp2c9 = 0.95, an activity score of 0 leaves 5% of E-3174 formation via CYP3A4, i.e. a ~20-fold rise in the losartan/E-3174 ratio. Yasar observed 30-fold in plasma — but in a single *3/*3 subject, so the true value is very uncertain. The model deliberately under-shoots rather than over-shoots. The heterozygote predictions (AS 1.5 -> 1.14x ratio; AS 1.0 -> 1.35x) are LOWER than Yasar's observed 2-3x for *1/*3 and *2/*3, meaning the linear activity-score mapping understates heterozygote effect. This is a known, documented limitation, not an oversight.

population_frequencies._method: CPIC 'Phenotype frequency' sheet, activity-score rows summed into phenotype bins (NM = AS 2; IM = AS 1.0 + 1.5; PM = AS 0 + 0.5).
population_frequencies.uzbekistan_note: NOT_FOUND — no Uzbekistan-specific CYP2C9 frequency data located. Central/South Asian carries a notably higher poor-metaboliser fraction (3.8%) than East Asian (0.6%), so the choice of proxy group materially changes how often the losartan non-responder scenario appears in a sampled population.

CYP3A4_CYP3A5.rationale: There is no CPIC-level actionable genotype recommendation for amlodipine. Modelling a CYP3A5 genotype effect on amlodipine would give the demo a pharmacogenomic claim the evidence does not support. Instead, CYP3A capacity is exposed as a free multiplier (default 1.0) so that inhibitor/inducer scenarios and the hepatic-impairment preset can act on it.

prov.basis: Absence of a CPIC guideline for amlodipine was confirmed by the CPIC guideline index; this is a negative finding, stated as such rather than filled with an invented effect size.

reference_individuals._note: Sanity anchors. If the pipeline is fed these inputs it must reproduce approximately these outputs; research/06-VALIDATION.md (Agent E) should turn this into a test.

icrp_reference_male.discrepancy_note: Nadler under-predicts ICRP blood volume by ~6% and therefore plasma volume by ~12%. The model's plasma volume nonetheless sits inside the NBME 25-43 mL/kg reference interval. Documented rather than fudged.

icrp_regional_blood_flow_pct_of_cardiac_._prov_stated: ICRP 89 section 7.7.2 p.142, 'Reference values for regional blood volumes and blood flow rates in adults'
icrp_regional_blood_flow_pct_of_cardiac_.use: Agent F can bind organ perfusion animation directly to cardiac_output_L_min multiplied by these fractions.

rules_engine_binding._purpose: Agent C's data/rules.json addresses patient state through its own namespaced vocabulary (`labs.*`, `vitals.*`, `demographic`, `phenotype`, `condition`). This section is the single authoritative translation between that vocabulary and the state-variable ids in this file. The coding agent must resolve every rule atom through this map. If a key is missing here, the rule cannot fire and that is a defect to report, not to paper over.
rules_engine_binding._contract: resolve(namespacedKey) -> { stateVar: string|null, transform?: string, status: 'bound'|'external_input'|'unmodelled' }

egfr_ml_min_1_73.note: The 1.73 m^2-INDEXED value, which is what guideline thresholds are written against. Do NOT bind this to egfr_absolute_mL_min.

serum_lithium_mmol_l.note: User-entered only. The twin has no lithium PK and must not display a predicted lithium level.

phenotype._note: Agent C's rules compare phenotype against the short codes PM / IM / NM / UM. This file's pipeline produces long names. Apply this transform.

cyp2d6.transform_caveat: Indeterminate is mapped to NM so that a rule does not silently fail to fire. The UI must show 'phenotype indeterminate — treated as normal metabolizer' rather than asserting NM.

cyp3a4.note: No actionable CYP3A4/5 genotype is modelled — see pharmacogenomic_presets.CYP3A4_CYP3A5. Any rule keyed on cyp3a4 phenotype will therefore only ever match NM. Agent C should key CYP3A interactions on co-medication (drug_class cyp3a4_inhibitor_strong), not on phenotype.

condition_keys._note: Every `condition` key Agent C's rules use, and where it resolves. `preset` keys carry physiological modifiers; `flag` keys are booleans with no physiology (allergies, enzyme deficiencies, dietary status) — deliberately so, because inventing haemodynamic shifts for a sulfonamide allergy would be fabrication.

acute_decompensated_hf.note: An acute state the twin does not simulate; it gates rules only. If it is set, the UI should say the simulation does not represent decompensation.

cardiogenic_shock.note: Out of scope for a resting-steady-state twin; rules gate only.

anuria.linked_state: Should be mutually exclusive with urine_output_mL_day > 100; the UI should enforce that.

severe_bradycardia.linked_state: heart_rate_bpm; the UI should derive this from HR rather than let the two disagree.

low_sodium_diet.note: Dietary sodium is not simulated — see validity_limits.not_modelled. This is a rules flag for the excipient sodium-content rule only.

risk_channels._purpose: Agent C's `risk_set` effect writes to `risk.<name>`. This is the registry of every such channel, so the engine has a typed place to store them and Agent F has a fixed list to bind animation to. Values are probabilities in [0,1] unless marked otherwise.

_prov.basis: These are model output channels, not measured physiology. Their baseline and drug-driven values are set by Agent C's rules, which carry their own citations. This registry contributes only the names, ranges and organ bindings.

channels.note: Rare and abrupt; represented as a probability only, not as a physiological trajectory.
NOT a graded risk in this model. It is the output of an absolute contraindication rule and must be rendered as a hard block, never as a percentage.

channels.horizon: long only — meaningless on an acute run

machine_readable_physiology._note: Bake this at build time from the US EPA httk TSVs rather than fetching at runtime. Values below were downloaded and parsed on 2026-08-17. Volumes are L per kg body weight; flows are mL/min per kg^(3/4) — multiply by Math.pow(weight_kg, 0.75) to get mL/min for an individual.

_volume_prov.from: httk cites ILSI-RSI 1994 in-band for every human organ volume row.

flow_prov.from: httk cites ILSI-RSI 1994 rather than Davies and Morris for this one row.

cross_check_at_70kg.verdict: httk reproduces the textbook GFR of 125 mL/min and a plasma volume of 3.0 L exactly, and its liver fraction (25.9%) matches ICRP 89's 25.5%. Its kidney fraction (22.1%) sits between ICRP's 19% and the 20-25% usually quoted.

discrepancy_with_icrp.cardiac_output: httk's allometric form gives 5.60 L/min at 70 kg; ICRP 89 states 6.5 L/min for the 73 kg reference male. That is a 14% difference and it is real, not an error: httk uses a Davies-and-Morris allometric average across a mixed population, while ICRP defines a single sex-specific reference individual.
discrepancy_with_icrp.resolution: This model uses the ICRP sex-specific BSA-scaled value (derivation_pipeline step 19) as primary, because sex-specific cardiac output matters for a twin whose user picks a sex. The httk allometric form is retained as a cross-check and as the fallback if a sex-agnostic scaling is ever wanted: cardiac_output_mL_min = 231.4 * Math.pow(weight_kg, 0.75). The engine must not mix the two.

machine_readable_physiology.use_for_agent_f: The organ table above is the direct binding surface for the organ animation: perfusion of organ X at time t = flow_mL_min_per_kg_0_75[X] * weight_kg^0.75 * (cardiac_output_L_min(t) / cardiac_output_L_min(baseline)). That gives every rendered organ a numerically defensible, citable perfusion value that responds to the drug.

validity_limits.population: Adults 18-95. No paediatric maturation, no neonatal or geriatric-frailty-specific PK.
not_modelled: Pulmonary circulation and right-heart mechanics — a single systemic loop only.
Regional autoregulation (cerebral, coronary, renal myogenic) — organ flows are fixed fractions of cardiac output, except where a preset overrides them.
Acid-base chemistry beyond a bicarbonate state variable.
Circadian rhythm in blood pressure — no dipper/non-dipper pattern.
Sodium and water intake as an input; dietary sodium is folded into the baseline rather than simulated.
Any drug outside the five modelled substances, including the patient's existing background therapy.
Pharmacodynamic tolerance beyond the explicit RAAS and baroreflex counter-regulation.

invalid_when: extremes of muscle mass (amputation, bodybuilding, severe sarcopenia)
equation_validity.ui_action: Show the eGFR greyed out with an explicit 'not valid in this patient' badge rather than hiding it.

invalid_when: oedematous states including HFrEF congestion and pregnancy
heart rate above about 100 bpm, where the systolic fraction of the cardiac cycle grows and the 1/3 weighting under-estimates MAP
equation_validity.ui_action: None; error is a few mmHg.

invalid_when: large wave-reflection differences between central and peripheral pressure
equation_validity.ui_action: None; it is a lumped estimate by design.

hard_output_clamps._purpose: The engine must clamp these before rendering. An unclamped model can produce a negative blood pressure and a judge will see it.

prov.basis: Chosen just outside the range of values compatible with life so that the clamp only fires on a numerical failure, never on a physiologically meaningful extreme. A clamp firing should raise a visible engine warning.

validity_limits.disclaimer: PilSim is a research and education simulator. Its virtual human is a lumped-parameter approximation calibrated to population reference values, not to any individual. It cannot predict what a drug will do in a real patient, it has not been validated against clinical outcomes, and it must not be used to prescribe, withhold, or adjust therapy.
